title: Reconcile rate-window semantics across deployments to stop cascading tenant throttles
creator: Marcel Ortega
description:
Summary:
A production regression in the new quota/burst policy rollout caused mismatch in how 'burst window' and 'refill rate' were interpreted between the public gateway (hosted) and the sidecar proxies used in Dedicated/Private. The difference (gateway using a sliding-window token-bucket, sidecars using fixed-window buckets) allowed tenants to exhaust global capacity in short spikes, cascade fallback logic, and surface opaque 429s to multiple customers. Several customers escalated to Support (CS-2219, CS-2224) and we saw elevated 5xx/429 rates in the metric dashboard during the outage window.

Timeline & impact:
- 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC: rollout of quota-policy v3.2 (contains change to burst handling semantics).
- 2026-03-09 02:38 UTC: initial alerts from customer-facing SLOs and Grafana (rate-limit 429 spike). Link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/rate-limits?from=2026-03-09T02:00Z&to=2026-03-09T03:00Z
- 2026-03-09 02:45 UTC: Support tickets CS-2219, CS-2224 created.
- 2026-03-09 03:05 UTC: mitigation — rollback quota-policy v3.2 on hosted and push emergency hotfix to Dedicated control-plane to re-enable previous token-bucket semantics.

Root cause (short):
- Two components interpreted burst/window differently: the gateway uses a sliding token-bucket (refill continuously), sidecar proxies used a fixed-window implementation (refill at window boundaries). The policy conversion layer introduced in v3.2 normalized the policy object but accidentally preserved the sidecar semantics in hosted paths. The net effect: tenants received double-counted burst allowances for short intervals when requests touched mixed components, letting sudden spikes bypass intended micro-throttles and then triggering global safeguards.

Actions taken so far (work performed):
- Emergency rollback of v3.2 on hosted completed at 2026-03-09 03:20 UTC (Marcel O., Jonah K.).
- Hotfix PR merged for sidecar policy parser to explicitly map to sliding-bucket semantics used by gateway: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345 (merged 2026-03-09 03:50 UTC, author: Aisha Patel).
- Temporary per-tenant grace window disabled and global-burst-cap enforced while team completed testing.
- Runbook updated to include a checklist for policy semantic compatibility across components.

Current plan (next steps):
1) Stabilize: finish QA of the unified policy library that canonicalizes "window" semantics across all runtimes; target merge to main by 2026-03-15. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 (WIP).
2) Add automated e2e tests that exercise mixed-path requests (hosted gateway -> dedicated sidecar -> private proxy) with synthetic tenants to validate burst/refill behavior; add to CI gate.
3) Backfill telemetry: publish a compact metric that shows 'policy-semantics-version' per request path to help detect drift.
4) Postmortem: produce customer-facing summary and internal RCA doc; assign to Marcel (lead) and Aisha (engineering fix owner). Draft will be ready by 2026-03-17.

Open questions & tradeoffs discussed:
- Option A: strictly enforce sliding-window semantics everywhere. Pros: consistent UX, fewer surprises. Cons: requires coordinated rollout on private on-prem proxies (customers without auto-updates) and may need migration knobs.
- Option B: support both semantics but add explicit conversion/compat layer per deployment type. Pros: less customer disruption for on-prem. Cons: higher long-term maintenance and slower reasoning about quotas.
Decision so far: choose Option A for short-term correctness (consistent semantics) and implement a compatibility shim for on-prem customers (Option B deferred to Q2 2026 as a migration path). Document decisions in the design note: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RINF/Quota+Semantics+Rationalization

Testing & verification:
- Unit tests added to runtime-policy module for token-bucket sliding behavior (coverage +12%).
- Integration smoke in staging: synthetic workload shows no 429 spikes across mixed-path scenarios. Staging run: 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC (logs: https://logs.redwood.com/goto/abcd-token-bucket-smoke).

Follow-ups (post-release):
- Create a blocking e2e test in the pre-merge CI for release branches.
- Communicate change and mitigation status to affected customers and CS leads (owner: Elaine Park).
- Schedule a migration tracker for on-prem/private customers that cannot auto-update; provide an agent-level patch and runbook.

Acceptance criteria (for Done):

- CI e2e test added and green on release-1.21 branch.
- On-prem compatibility plan documented and outreach scheduled for impacted customers.
- Customer-facing incident summary published and CS tickets marked resolved with follow-ups.
